### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A19, A20 and A25 were essentially unobserved (0 of 200 traces for A19 and A25, 1 of 200 for A20); in the later window each occurs in roughly 30–38 of 100 traces (A19 about 76 of 200, A25 about 69 of 200, A20 about 59 of 200), at most once per trace. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003]
- In the later window the three sit between A41 and A26: about 33 of 100 observed outgoing transitions of A41 now go to A19, about 30 to A25 and about 24 to A20, while the direct A41→A26 transition fell from about 82 of 100 earlier to about 2 of 100 (based on roughly 200 outgoing transitions per window); A19's outgoing transitions lead to A26 in about 95 of 100 cases and A25's in about 90 of 100. Earlier, A19 and A25 had no observed outgoing transitions at all. [DIR002, DIR003, DIR004]
- Relational evidence agrees: in the later window A41 precedes A19, A20 or A25 in about 28–38 of 100 traces — essentially always when they occur — and each of the three precedes A26 in about 28–38 of 100 traces, again essentially always; earlier, none of the three ever co-occurred with A41 or A26. [REL003, REL004, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009]
- The three behave as mutually exclusive alternatives: each pair occurs together in only about 1–3 of 200 later traces, and each pair's "neither" share (about 29–34 of 100) matches the third activity's participation, so roughly 99 of 100 later traces contain exactly one of the three. [REL001, REL002, REL005]
- Positions fit this picture: A19 and A25 appear around 35–37% of the way through the trace, and A26 — still present in every trace in both windows — shifted slightly later (mean relative position 0.37 to 0.40). [POS001, POS003, POS004]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that, in the later window, a choice among three mutually exclusive activities — A19, A20 and A25 — is executed between A41 and A26, with essentially every case running exactly one of them after A41 and before A26, whereas in the earlier window none of the three were observed and A41 led predominantly directly to A26. Screening produced 20 qualifying items against roughly 0.5 expected without change, far beyond what a stable process yields, and the hypothesis is directly and consistently supported on both sides of the relation: the activities' appearance at 30–38% participation, the rerouting of A41's outgoing transitions towards them, their near-invariable succession to A26, and A26's slight positional shift. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, REL003, REL004, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, POS004]

Limitations: the one-alternative-per-case reading rests on very low co-occurrence counts (about 1–3 traces per pair), and positions are event positions rather than clock time, so the exact placement of the new steps is approximate; 0 occurrences in 200 earlier traces makes pure sampling variation implausible, but the evidence cannot show whether the three activities are new to the process or previously unsampled in this segment. A competing explanation the evidence cannot fully rule out is that this is one part of a broader rerouting touching other activities as well, since not all changed transitions are explained by the A41–A26 relation. [REL001, REL002, REL005, DIR001]

Other differences: A02's outgoing transitions were redistributed — A26 fell from about 26 of 100 observed outgoing transitions to unobserved, A16 rose from about 9 to about 18 of 100, and many previously unseen successors now each take about 2 of 100; with only about 35 versus 44 observed transitions, these proportions are weak. [DIR001]
